ca_raceway_rock.blurb: Raceway Rock is a sloping apron of water-polished stone rising from the edge of a sandy wash in the San Bernardino Mountains, a short way along the Cajon Wash boulders. It has nine bouldering problems, all at the easiest grade, VB. The stone is decent low down, but around the ten foot mark it breaks into loose rubble, so the problems stay short and climbers downclimb or jump off rather than topping out. The base sits right beside the track through the wash, which makes it a handy stop for a warm-up or for newer boulderers. Deep soft sand lies along stretches of the track.

ca_poopship_destroyer.blurb: Poopship Destroyer is a small creekside bouldering spot beside Highway 33 near Ojai, tucked just below a quarry. The boulders are water-polished sandstone, and the creek and a swimming hole sit right alongside. There are nine problems, running from about V3 up to V8, with a cluster around V5 and a couple of hard lines at the top of the range. Boulderers drop in from the roadside over a short jumble of rock. The landings are uneven in places, so extra pads and spotters are useful.

ca_television_wall.blurb: Television Wall is a small face on a hillside shoulder above Group Campsite 1 in the Sheep Pass area of Joshua Tree National Park. It has nine routes, six on trad gear and three set up for top rope. The grades start at scramble level and reach 5.11, with most between 5.7 and 5.10. A one-bolt face line runs up the middle, and a knife-edge arete with a partly detached block marks the left side. The stone is blocky in places and could use more cleaning, yet it feels solid. A rocky gully and a well-worn trail lead up from the campsite to the base.

ca_power_boulder.blurb: Power Boulder is the biggest block in a small cluster of boulders near June Lake in the Eastern Sierra, easy to pick out by its undercut shape. Its nine problems are generally steep and powerful, a different flavour from the slabbier boulder about ten yards south. Grades run from V1 up to V11, with most of them between V1 and V5 and a few harder lines above. The block stands only a short stroll north of where cars stop. Spring and fall tend to give better conditions here than hot summer days.

ca_the_great_roof.blurb: The Great Roof is the section of the Mill, a basalt crag on the rim above Mill Creek Canyon in northeastern California, that sits under and through a huge roof. It lies between the Amphitheater and the Main Wall, a short way along from the top of the approach trail. There are nine sport routes, from 5.10 into the 5.12 range, with most split between 5.11 and 5.12. The lines are dead vertical. The roof keeps most of them dry, so it can be climbed in light rain, and the left side drops into shade later in the day.

ca_torque_spanner_boulder.blurb: This is a single boulder in the Camp 4 area on the north side of Yosemite Valley, southwest of Yosemite Lodge. It holds nine bouldering problems, from VB up to V8. Several of them are at V0 or below, with a couple around V6 and one V8 at the top. To find it, follow the trail east from the wine boulder to the fork where one branch heads to the waterfall and the other to Swan Slab; the boulder stands to the left of the path.

ca_the_dungeon.blurb: The Dungeon is a recently revived sport crag in the Mount Shasta area, reached from Everitt Memorial Highway. It has nine bolted routes from 5.9 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 and 5.11, and the hardware is modern, with lower-off anchors on every line. Shade covers the wall all day, which makes it a better fit for late spring, summer and fall than for cold months. Beyond the end of the dirt road the walk is about half a mile, on a trail that passes a short bolted wall and a narrow boulder tunnel before it reaches the top of the crag and drops to the base.

ca_pokom_boulder.blurb: Pokom Boulder is one large boulder in the Lone Valley area of northeastern California, with climbable faces on every side. Nine routes mix trad and sport, seven of them on gear, running from 5.5 up to 5.12 with most between 5.5 and 5.10. Two sets of anchors on top let you rig a top rope on almost every line, and a few pieces of protection are handy as directionals. The lead lines on gear need only a single rack to three inches. It is among the southernmost formations in the valley, and the top of the boulder is visible from the road.
